items.question: We ___ a great film last night.
explanations: ‘Watch’ is present simple. ‘Last night’ is a finished time, so use the past: ‘watched’.
Correct! Regular verbs add -ed in the past simple: ‘watched’. ‘Last night’ is a finished time.
‘Watches’ is the he/she/it present form, and ‘we’ doesn’t take it. A finished action needs ‘watched’.
‘Have watched’ (present perfect) can’t go with a finished time like ‘last night’.

items.question: She ___ to Paris in 2019.
explanations: ‘Go’ is irregular, so it doesn’t take -ed. The past is ‘went’.
‘Goes’ is present simple. ‘In 2019’ is finished: ‘went’.
‘Has gone’ (present perfect) can’t go with ‘in 2019’. Use ‘went’.
Correct! ‘Go’ is irregular: its past simple is ‘went’.

items.question: They ___ the message yesterday.
explanations: ‘Don’t see’ is present. ‘Yesterday’ is a finished time: ‘didn’t see’.
‘Weren’t seeing’ is past continuous, for an action in progress. A single finished event takes ‘didn’t see’.
Correct! Negatives use didn’t + base verb: ‘didn’t see’. ‘Didn’t’ already carries the past.
‘Haven’t seen’ (present perfect) can’t go with ‘yesterday’.

items.question: ___ the thunder last night?
explanations: ‘Do you hear’ is present. ‘Last night’ is a finished time: ‘Did you hear’.
‘Have you heard’ (present perfect) can’t go with ‘last night’.
‘Are you hearing’ is present continuous, for right now.
Correct! Past questions use Did + subject + base verb: ‘Did you hear…?’.

items.question: I ___ him at the station yesterday.
explanations: ‘See’ is present. A completed action yesterday takes ‘saw’.
Correct! A finished-time expression like ‘yesterday’ takes the past simple: ‘saw’.
‘Have seen’ (present perfect) can’t go with ‘yesterday’.
‘Will see’ is future, but ‘yesterday’ is past.

items.question: He ___ a new car last month.
explanations: ‘Buy’ is irregular, so it doesn’t take -ed. The past is ‘bought’, not ‘buyed’.
‘Buys’ is present simple. ‘Last month’ is finished: ‘bought’.
‘Has bought’ (present perfect) can’t go with a finished time like ‘last month’.
Correct! ‘Buy’ is irregular: the past simple is ‘bought’.

items.question: Last night I ___ for my exam until midnight.
explanations: When a verb ends in consonant + -y, the -y changes to -ied: ‘studied’, not ‘studyed’.
‘Studies’ is present simple. ‘Last night’ is finished: ‘studied’.
Correct! Consonant + -y becomes -ied: study → studied.
‘Have studied’ (present perfect) can’t go with ‘last night’.

items.question: We ___ in Girona when we were children.
explanations: ‘Live’ is present simple. A finished past state takes ‘lived’.
‘Have lived’ (present perfect) suggests it continues now, but ‘when we were children’ is finished.
Correct! A past state that is now finished uses the past simple: ‘lived’.
‘Are living’ is present continuous, about now. The finished past takes ‘lived’.

items.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have seen her two years ago.
I see her two years ago.
I’m seeing her two years ago.
I saw her two years ago.
explanations: ‘Ago’ marks a finished time, so the present perfect (‘have seen’) is impossible.
‘See’ is present. ‘Two years ago’ is in the past: ‘saw’.
‘I’m seeing’ is present continuous. ‘Two years ago’ needs the past simple: ‘saw’.
Correct! ‘Ago’ marks a finished time, so we use the past simple: ‘saw’.

items.question: When the phone rang, I ___ it immediately.
explanations: ‘Answer’ is present simple. The action happened in the past: ‘answered’.
‘Have answered’ is present perfect. With a finished past sequence, use the past simple: ‘answered’.
Correct! Two completed past actions in sequence (rang, then answered) both take the past simple.
‘Was answering’ suggests an action already in progress, but answering was a quick reaction to the ring.

items.question: She ___ her keys on the bus yesterday. (leave)
Did you went to the party?
answers: Did you go to the party?
Did you go to the party
Did you go to that party
items.explanation: After ‘did’ the main verb stays in its base form: ‘go’. Remember the question mark.

items.question: I didn’t saw him.
items.explanation: After ‘did not’ / ‘didn’t’ the main verb stays in its base form: ‘see’.
